1.explanation:
• audits/byte-efficiency/uses-response-compression.js: Contains the audit logic that inspects network records and determines which text responses are “uncompressed.” 
• audits/byte-efficiency/uses-response-compression-test.js: Provides unit tests and sample networkRecords for this audit, a starting point to reproduce and understand the failure case.  
• gather/gatherers/dobetterweb/response-compression-test.js: Tests the gatherer that captures response compression data from the page load; essential for understanding how compression headers are read and passed to the audit.  
• gather/network-recorder-test.js: Shows how raw networkRecords are recorded from DevTools logs (including headers and encodedDataLength), which feeds into the compression audit.  
• gather/devtools-log-test.js: Demonstrates how DevTools protocol messages are processed into the driver artifact; useful to trace the path from real network traffic (with gzip headers) into the networkRecords used by the audit.
1.bug_scenario: The bug appears in the Lighthouse “Enable text compression” audit. In the audit’s UI you expand “View Details” under “Enable text compression” and see a table of text-based resources (here several calls to “/api/blob”) with columns “Uncompressed resource URL”, “Original”, and “GZIP Savings”. Lighthouse is flagging these responses as uncompressed (showing original sizes ~29–30 KB and GZIP savings ~23 KB), even though DevTools’ Network panel and a curl request both report a “Content-Encoding: gzip” header. In other words, Lighthouse is erroneously classifying already-gzipped responses as uncompressed. Key UI elements involved are the audit list item, the expand/collapse chevron, and the details table of resource URLs and size columns.
